name: Stinnett Run

shape.recipe: 0–30 h: wind from W 65 km/h, RH 12%, head 11 km/h, LB 7. Hour 30: cold front, wind from NE 45 km/h, the south flank becomes the head running SW toward Pampa, LB 4.

events.text: Pole failure on the Xcel corridor ignites cured grass north-east of Stinnett.
Head reaches the Canadian outskirts.
Borger refinery flank exposed.
Frontal passage: wind swings to the north-east; the south flank becomes the head toward Pampa.
Crews hold the head on plowed wheat north of Pampa.

exposureText: 45 km of Xcel line (502 poles), Turkey Track, 590 homes in Canadian and Stinnett, 4,520 cattle; the Borger refinery on the flank at h14 (monitored, outside the P50)

assetsInPath.note: Flank exposed at h14; monitored, outside the P50 band

shape.recipe: Wind from N 25 km/h gusting 50, head 1.6 km/h, LB 2. Fingers on bearings 200°, 225°, 250° up the draws toward Lake Austin. Spotting 120 m. Barriers: Lake Austin (hard), RM 620 (70%). Slope ×1.4 on the fingers.

events.text: Power-line arcs at three spans on RM 620 ignite the juniper strip.
Three fingers run up the draws toward Lake Austin.
Spot fires land 120 m ahead of the fingers.
The eastern finger reaches Lake Austin; the lake stops the head.
Engines hold the flanks at the ridge roads.

name: Lost Pines

shape.recipe: Wind from N 22 km/h, head 2.2 km/h, LB 2.5; three ignitions merge by h48 into a clover-leaf; spotting 0.8–2 km ahead every 6 h; five-day burn with night slowdown.

events.text: Three ignitions in the loblolly blocks, 2 km apart.
First spot fires land 0.8–2 km ahead of the heads.
Night slowdown; the three heads run again with the afternoon wind.
The three lobes merge into a clover-leaf.
Five days in: crews hold the three heads north of SH 71.

exposureText: 409 homes, $131M TIV, 6.8 km of the Bluebonnet spur

name: Carbon double-header

shape.recipe: 0–13 h: wind from SW 40 km/h, head 4 km/h, LB 4 (ellipse pointing NE). Hour 13 (21:00): shift to wind from N 30 km/h, east flank becomes head, runs south over Carbon, LB 2 → T-shape.

events.text: Conductor contact on the Oncor feeder, 08:00.
Head runs north-east under a 40 km/h south-westerly.
Wind shift at 21:00: north wind turns the east flank into a new head.
Second head runs south over Carbon.
Held on the Carbon ranch roads.

exposureText: 155 homes in Carbon, 8 km of the Oncor feeder (84 poles)

name: Crabapple II

shape.recipe: Wind shifting: SW 35 → W 50 → NW 40 km/h at h0/h6/h14, head 1.2 km/h, LB 2.5; fingers on each wind bearing, pockets between → egg with alternating fingers.

events.text: Ignition on a ranch track in the oak-juniper savanna.
Wind veers to the west; a second finger runs east.
North-west wind: the third finger turns south-east toward town.
Pockets between the fingers burn in.
Held at the north boundary of the subdivision.

exposureText: 34 homes, 60 outbuildings; the PEC feeder in the tail band

shape.recipe: Wind from S 20 km/h, slope ×1.8 uphill (bearings 330–30°), head 1.0 km/h, LB 1.8; lake arms as hard barriers so the perimeter wraps into a crescent; multi-day.

events.text: Ignition in the juniper breaks above the lake.
Head runs uphill to the north under a south wind.
Lake arms stop the head; the fire wraps along the shore.
Second burning day: flanks back down to the coves.
Held at the shoreline and the peninsula roads.

name: Matador–Waggoner outbreak

shape.recipe: Wind from SW 55 km/h, RH 7%, head 8 km/h, LB 4 for 7 h then wind eases to 25 km/h; Caprock escarpment (hard) and plowed cotton (hard) block the west flank → lopsided teardrop.

events.text: Ignitions in the ranch quadrant under a 55 km/h south-westerly, RH 7%.
Caprock escarpment and plowed cotton stop the west flank.
Wind eases to 25 km/h; the head slows.
East flank runs across the Tongue River pastures.
State plan: engines hold the teardrop at the county roads.

analogue.name: Southern Plains outbreak, Texas and Oklahoma

exposureText: 9,597 ha of pasture, 61 km of fencing, 5,520 cattle, 3 ranch headquarters and camps

name: Colorado City ROW

shape.recipe: Wind from W 35 km/h, head 5 km/h, LB 3; fingers along the ROW bearing 75°; caliche pads as islands (30 patches); Delek refinery and 60 Roscoe turbines on the flank.

events.text: Line-to-tree contact at a well pad on the pipeline ROW.
Fingers run along the ROW on bearing 75°.
Caliche pads stay unburned as islands.
Roscoe turbines on the south flank.
Held at the county road; pump stations defended.

exposureText: 37 km of the Basin pipeline with 3 pump stations; the Delek refinery and the Roscoe turbines on the flanks

assetsInPath.note: On the upwind flank; monitored, outside all bands
Turbines about 15 km off the south flank; monitored, outside all bands

name: Osage patch-burn

shape.recipe: Wind from S 45 km/h, head 11 km/h, LB 5; last year’s patch burns as islands (ten blocks of varied size) so the perimeter shows bays and islands and halts at burned patches.

events.text: Ignition in the south unit under a 45 km/h south wind.
Head reaches last season’s patch burns and splits around them.
Bays form where patches reach into the flanks; burned blocks stay as islands.
Out of fuel against the patch mosaic.

exposureText: 1,395 ha of tallgrass, 1,905 bison and cattle, 3 structures

name: Stillwater cigars

shape.recipe: Wind from SW 90 km/h gusting 130, RH 8%, three downed-line ignitions 1.5 km apart, head 16 km/h, LB 8 (cap) → three parallel cigars for 5 h, then wind eases to 30 km/h and they merge sideways.

events.text: Three downed-line ignitions on the OG&E feeder, 1.5 km apart.
Three parallel cigars run north-east under a 90 km/h south-westerly.
Wind eases to 30 km/h; the cigars start to widen.
The three runs merge sideways into one front.
Held at the section-line roads south-west of Stillwater.

exposureText: 295 homes, $77M TIV, 18 km of the OG&E feeder and its Stillwater substation; Cushing tank farm 31 h away on the flank (monitored, outside all bands)

assetsInPath.note: On the flank, 31 h away at forecast spread; monitored, outside all bands
